page.layout: One column of running text on a single printed page. Running head "LATINA." centred at the top, page number "133" at top right. No marginal notes. Two headings, each centred and italic, set between paragraphs. Gathering signature at the foot, left of centre.

main_text.p: Adverbia, O,Proh,& Hem. regunt Nominativum, Accusativum vel Vocativum.
Vah regit Nominativum: Heu regit Nominativum vel Accusativum: Hei & Væ regunt Dativum: Heus, Ah & Ohe regunt Vocativum. Usus spectandus.
main_text.head: Quæ est tricesimanona Regula?
main_text.p: Unum & triginta Adverbia sunt, quæ Accusativum regunt, ut, Ad, zu. Apud, bey. Ante, vor. Adversus, zuwider. Cis, disseit. Citra, disseit. Ultra, vber/jenseit. Intra, in/innerhalb. Extra, draussen. Circum, vmb. Circa, herumb. Circiter, vmb oder bey/ad tempus & numerum referrtur. Contra, wider. Erga, gegen. Inter, zwischen/vnter. Infra, vnder. Supra, droben/ober. Juxta, bey/nach. Ob, von wegen. Per, durch. Prope, bey oder nahe. Præter, ohn/vber/wider. Propter, von wegen. Post, hinder. Penes, in gewalt/bey. Secundum, bey/nach. Trans, hinüber/jenseit. Pone, hinder/zu rück. Secus, neben/bey. Usq; bis. Versus, gegen. Ex his nonnulla absq; casu usurpantur. Gerundium in Dum est Accusativi loco: ut, Mitto illum ad speculandum arcem.
main_text.head: Quæ est quadragesima Regula?
main_text.p: Quatuordecim Adverbia sunt, quæ Ablativum regunt: ut, A, von/nach/wider. Ab, von. Abs, von. Absque, ohn. Cum, mit. Clam, ohn wissen. Coram, vor/in beiwesen. De, von/auß/von wegen. E, auß. Ex, auß. Pro, vor/in/nach/von wegen/für. Præ, vor/von wegen. Sine, ohn/ & Tenues, biß an/quod semper postponitur. A & E regunt Ablativum incipientem a consona: ut, a te. a Jove, e conspectu. Ab regit Ablativum incipientem a Vocali vel L, vel R, vel jod: ut, ab alio, ab lege, ab Rege, ab Jove. Abs regit Ablativum incipientem a Q vel T: ut, Abs quivis homine, abs te. Græcum est, crurum tenus, Virgil. Cumarum tenus, in Epistol.

page.notes: Several German glosses are set in black letter and are marked with <bl>. The marks in the text, such as "zu" for Ad, were read with some uncertainty. The word after "Sine," is printed as "Tenues" or "Tenus", and I read it as "Tenues". The printed page number is at the top right, and the signature "i 3" is at the foot.
